# GTM Growth — product reference

Reviewed 2026-11-14 against the repository. See the linked capability registry for detailed implementation boundaries.

## Purpose and journey

GTM Growth is an Apache-2.0 workspace for public SEO/GEO evidence and authorised customer data. Its product journey is Diagnose → Understand → Act → Measure → Grow. A bilingual website and console, CLI and MCP interfaces support different users of the same domain modules.

The marketing reading track explains customer decisions, outputs, ownership and evidence limits. The technical track explains the runtime, connector contracts, scoped access and deployment. Both public guides exist in English and French.

## Evidence boundaries

- Public page reads return GEO v1/SEO evidence. They do not include private GA4 or Search Console reports and do not measure actual AI citations.
- Buyer question planning starts from observed product/service data and confirmed brand, buyer and need. Its questions are hypotheses. Saving a question does not run a model collection.
- AI visibility can use source-labelled imports or explicitly requested supported API collection. Provider credentials and possible usage costs apply. Gemini collection is disabled.
- Search, analytics, Social and commerce observations must retain their source, period and scope. Commerce totals can mix currencies and denominator scopes; review orders before reporting revenue or attribution.
- CRM timelines use exact identity associations scoped to tenant and source/store. Unmatched events remain unlinked. Aggregate GA4/Social metrics and IP addresses do not prove contact identity. Manual declarations, source assertions and observed store events remain distinguishable.

## Runtime and integration

The core uses Node.js, TypeScript and Express, with SQLite stores for module state. The authenticated console uses Keycloak, whose deployment has a separate PostgreSQL database. Client API contracts check tenant membership, module roles and resource access. The general shared-token MCP endpoint is an operator interface; a caller-supplied tenantId is not proof of membership.

Google resources need explicit account/resource permissions. Shopify and PrestaShop require store configuration, encrypted credentials and ingestion setup. CRM collection must be enabled explicitly. Its reference integration does not mean a named third-party CRM is preconfigured.

Optional services have separate activation and acceptance steps: Node-RED for local jobs, ZenML/Postiz for Social, and Eve for authorised Slack reads. Installing the core does not configure those services.

## Actions and availability

Apply Mode currently provides previews. It does not apply arbitrary remote changes or provide operational rollback. WordPress drafts, supported GBP updates and Social scheduling use their own approval and execution contracts. Social publication requires setup, independent approval and explicit scheduling. No automatic outreach is implied.

The 42 AI visibility checks run live in the public read; the 4 browser-rendering checks need proof of site ownership, and the isolated renderer is not yet a public service. Named vendor CRM adapters remain future work. Self-hosted software is free; hosting and optional provider/model usage may cost money. Solo €39/month and Agency €149/month are pilot pricing hypotheses. Mollie checkout and subscription entitlements are inactive.

The primary site is served by Nginx on the existing OVH VPS. A repository push alone does not deploy. Release through the protected VPS workflow, then verify the live public site and separately qualify authorised source integrations.
